nameStory: The 'Resplendent' Running Crab Spider gets its glamorous name from its shimmering, almost metallic appearance that catches the light beautifully. Like other running crab spiders, it moves sideways and forward with impressive speed, using its crab-like leg positioning to dart across surfaces. The name 'praelustris' comes from Latin meaning 'very bright' or 'brilliant,' emphasizing this spider's eye-catching luster.
description: The Resplendent Running Crab Spider is a small, fast-moving hunter that doesn't build webs to catch prey. Instead, it relies on speed and stealth, darting across plant surfaces to ambush unsuspecting insects. This spider has a flattened, crab-like body with legs that extend sideways, allowing it to move in multiple directions with remarkable agility. Like other running crab spiders, it's relatively small but makes up for size with lightning-fast reflexes.

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Flattened, crab-like body that feels firm to the touch if gently handled, with legs extending sideways rather than directly beneath the body

idTips.label: Markings
idTips.description: Distinctive metallic or iridescent sheen that shifts and sparkles as it moves, creating an almost jewel-like appearance in good lighting

idTips.label: Behavior
idTips.description: Moves with quick, darting motions in multiple directions including sideways, freezing suddenly when startled before bolting to safety

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Small spider that could comfortably sit on a dime, with legs that don't feel delicate but rather sturdy for its size

idTips.label: Web
idTips.description: No web for catching prey - this is a free-roaming hunter that may leave behind single draglines of silk when moving

habitat: Found on vegetation including shrubs, low trees, and flowering plants where it hunts for small insects. Prefers areas with good sun exposure that highlight its metallic coloration, often seen on the undersides of leaves or bark surfaces in mixed woodlands and forest edges.

seasonality.spring: Adults become active as temperatures warm, beginning to hunt actively on emerging vegetation. Look for their characteristic quick movements on new leaves and branches.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period when adults are most visible and actively hunting. This is the best time to spot their distinctive metallic sheen in bright sunlight.
seasonality.fall: Mating season occurs with egg-laying following shortly after. Adults may be seen guarding their egg sacs on plant surfaces.
seasonality.winter: Adults typically die off with juveniles or eggs overwintering in protected locations under bark or leaf litter.

funFact: Despite being called a 'crab spider,' running crab spiders like this one can actually move forward just as easily as sideways, unlike true crab spiders which are more limited to lateral movement - making them the sports cars of the spider world!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with the Metallic Crab Spider (Philodromus marxi), but the Resplendent Running Crab Spider typically has a more brilliant, almost mirror-like sheen. Memory trick: 'Resplendent' means extra shiny - look for the spider that really catches your eye with its sparkle.
contextualKnowledge: With only 3 recorded observations in New England, this spider is either genuinely rare in the region or easily overlooked due to its small size and quick movements. Many running crab spiders are under-documented because they don't build obvious webs and their speed makes them challenging to observe closely.
compareHints: Compared to other Philodromus species in New England, the Resplendent Running Crab Spider stands out for its particularly brilliant metallic appearance - more lustrous than the Metallic Crab Spider and lacking the white stripes of the White-striped Running Crab Spider. While the Turf Running Spider prefers ground-level habitats, this species is more often found on above-ground vegetation where its shimmering colors are most visible.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Unlike its cousin the White-striped Running Crab Spider which has obvious white stripes, the metallic crab spider males are uniformly shiny without stripes.

The white-striped running crab spider is distinguished from its relatives by those prominent longitudinal white stripes - most other Philodromus species in New England have more subtle markings or different color patterns.

The Turf Running Spider differs from its Philodromus relatives primarily in habitat preference - while the Metallic Crab Spider tends toward trees and the White-striped Running Crab Spider prefers taller shrubs, the Turf Running Spider sticks to low vegetation and ground cover.

Among its Philodromus relatives in New England, the male's distinctive shiny black coloration with white edges makes it relatively easy to distinguish from the more uniformly colored Metallic Crab Spider or the striped patterns of the White-striped Running Crab Spider.
The Minute Running Crab Spider is significantly smaller than its relatives like the Metallic Crab Spider or White-striped Running Crab Spider, which are much more commonly encountered.
Philodromus exilis is notably more slender than the Metallic Crab Spider or White-striped Running Crab Spider, lacking the metallic sheen or distinct striping of those relatives.
